typical_symptoms: Downward curling and distortion of young leaves
Stunting of overall plant growth and young terminal shoots
Excretion of sticky honeydew covering leaf surface
Growth of dark sooty mold on honeydew-covered areas
Chlorosis or yellowing of foliage due to sap loss
visual_characteristics: Dense colonies of tiny, soft-bodied, pear-shaped insects on leaf undersides and stems
Glossy, wet-looking shiny residue (honeydew) on lower leaves
Blackish powdery layer (sooty mold) accumulating on upper leaf surfaces
lesion_characteristics: Microscopic feeding punctures causing localized chlorotic spotting
Leaf distortion rather than defined lesion margins
Variable size of affected distorted tissue depending on infestation severity
color_characteristics: Insects vary in color from light yellow-green to dark green, brown, or almost black
Leaves turn pale yellow to chlorotic green
Sooty mold turns honeydew-covered areas dark gray to velvety black
texture_characteristics: Sticky and glossy surface from honeydew
Wrinkled, puckered, and curled leaf blades
Velvety texture where black sooty mold establishes
spatial_patterns: Dense clusters along leaf veins and undersides
Concentrated infestations on young growing points and tender terminal leaves
Irregular spread across canopy as honeydew drips to lower foliage
distinguishing_features: Direct observation of small, oval/pear-shaped wingless or winged insects with posterior cornicles
Downward cupping of leaves combined with clear sticky honeydew and black sooty mold
Presence of cast nymphal skins (white exuviae) on leaf surfaces
